sermon.title: Government and Children 09/16/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer continues on children: natural parents must discipline by example, church leaders must rule their own homes, and when parents fail, government must help or hold them accountable, as in Deuteronomy 21. Rulers must be just, and when they are not, God brings a refining fire to correct a nation.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Statistics on divorce, single-parent households, immigration and abortion are kept as spoken and were not checked.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the men would not heed him. So the man took his concubine and brought her out to them. And they knew her and abused her all night until morning; and when the day began to break, they let her go. Then the woman came as the day was dawning, and fell down at the door of the man’s house where her master was, till it was light. When her master arose in the morning, and opened the doors of the house and went out to go his way, there was his concubine, fallen at the door of the house with her hands on the threshold. And he said to her, “Get up and let us be going.” But there was no answer. So the man lifted her onto the donkey; and the man got up and went to his place. When he entered his house he took a knife, laid hold of his concubine, and divided her into twelve pieces, limb by limb, and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel.

Then all the children of Israel, that is, all the people, went up and came to the house of God and wept. They sat there before the LORD and fasted that day until evening; and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

faqs.question: Does the Bible say to discipline with a club?
faqs.answer: No; a rod, not a club, and not your hand.

faqs.question: What does blameless mean?
faqs.answer: If they took you to court, there wouldn’t be enough evidence to convict you.

faqs.question: What does he say about legalizing marijuana and alcohol?
faqs.answer: Don’t follow that crowd; it destroys lives and families.

faqs.question: What does “stubborn” mean in Deuteronomy 21?
faqs.answer: Unmanageable and unwilling to change, like refractory material.

faqs.question: What does he say about pedophile sentences?
faqs.answer: They are not punished seriously and many offend again.

faqs.question: What does he say about pro-choice?
faqs.answer: The baby has no choice and should have an equal right.

faqs.question: How did his sons avoid college debt?
faqs.answer: He says they got their education for about $20,000.

faqs.question: What does he promise young people who make good choices?
